_comment: The markets this project originates, in the order the brief fixes them: the side (point spread)
first, then the total, then the moneyline. Each market carries the price-snapshot store columns
(opening and closing recorded as separate columns) and the origination columns (the model's fair
line, the market line, and the difference between them, published as separate columns).
Every value below is blank and flagged. The NFL publishes no machine-readable line, and no
official publisher releases an opening or closing number for this project. The only opening-line
file in the pinned dataset covers 2021 alone. A value that cannot be confirmed from an official
source is left blank, never inferred.

store_schema.name: price-snapshot store

columns.note: one of the three origination markets: side, total, ml
the game the snapshot belongs to
the side taken (e.g. home / away / over / under / favourite / underdog)
the point/total/margin number for the market, blank if unpublished
the American-odds price at that snapshot, blank if unpublished
the official publisher or pinned dataset commit the value came from
true only if an official publisher states the value

store_schema.rule: Opening and closing are stored as two separate rows per selection, never merged into one. A snapshot kind with no official value is stored as a blank row with verified=false and a flag, so the store shows what is missing rather than substituting a number.

origination_schema.name: origination table

columns.note: the model's own fair line for this market, blank unless computed and labelled recomputed
the published market line, blank unless an official source states it
fair_line minus market_line, published as its own column, blank if either input is blank
the official publisher or pinned dataset commit

origination_schema.rule: The fair line, the market line and the difference are three separate columns. The difference is never computed from a filled-in value: if either input is blank, the difference is blank too.

markets.name: Side (point spread)
markets.definition: A 2-way point-spread market: the chosen outcome must win by more, or lose by less, than the stated number of points. A whole-number line settles as a push if the margin equals the line.
markets.blank_reason: No official publisher releases a machine-readable side line, and the pinned open dataset supplies the closing line only as a Tier-3 source. No opening side line exists for this project.

markets.name: Total (points)
markets.definition: A total-points market: a 2-way market on the combined points scored, with Over and Under selections. A bet settles as a push when the total equals the stated number.
markets.blank_reason: No official publisher releases a machine-readable total line. The pinned open dataset is the only source and is Tier 3. No opening total line exists for this project.

markets.name: Moneyline
markets.definition: A 2-way moneyline market: a win-only wager on which selection wins the event. The favourite carries a minus sign (wager to win $100), the underdog a plus sign, and a tie settles as a push.
markets.blank_reason: No official publisher releases a machine-readable moneyline. The pinned open dataset is the only source and is Tier 3. No opening moneyline exists for this project.
